# Requirements Quality Checklist: GitLab Scope Selection

**Purpose**: Review whether Feature 004 requirements are complete, unambiguous, consistent, and reviewable before implementation.
**Created**: 2026-09-28
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Completeness and Scope Semantics

- [ ] CHK001 Are the prerequisites for discovery and adding selections distinguished clearly from the ability to inspect or remove saved rules when credentials are absent? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK002 Is the distinction between lazy hierarchy loading and complete reachability of every result/page clear enough to prevent either full-instance preloading or silent truncation? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002, FR-003, SC-002]
- [ ] CHK003 Is the meaning of a selected group explicit about descendant groups, future repositories, directly owned projects, and projects merely shared from elsewhere? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK004 Is individual repository selection clearly independent of parent-group selection, including the outcome when the covering group is later removed? [Completeness, Spec §FR-008, User Story 1 Scenario 6]
- [ ] CHK005 Is it unambiguous that overlapping rules are deduplicated for effective coverage while explicit group and repository intent remains separately editable? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, SC-003]
- [ ] CHK006 Are explicit, inherited/covered, partial, and unknown-unloaded tree states distinguishable without implying persistence of an unselected group? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009]
- [ ] CHK007 Does the specification make clear that only explicit group and repository rules persist, while expansion, filtering, and partial-selection presentation remain transient? [Completeness, Spec §FR-009, FR-010, FR-016]
- [ ] CHK008 Is the valid empty-scope outcome clearly separated from configuration enabled/disabled state and from any future execution eligibility rule? [Consistency, Spec §FR-017]

## Identity, Reconciliation, and Failure Behavior

- [ ] CHK009 Are stable entity identifiers always interpreted together with the originating GitLab instance identity, including same-ID collisions across instances? [Completeness, Spec §FR-010, FR-015]
- [ ] CHK010 Is the behavior for renamed or moved entities within the same instance clear, including preservation of the selection and refresh of descriptive metadata? [Clarity, Spec §FR-012, User Story 2 Scenario 1]
- [ ] CHK011 Does “unavailable or unresolved” sufficiently distinguish inaccessible/deleted entities from temporary reconciliation failures, and define what the user can do in each case? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013, FR-018]
- [ ] CHK012 Is it explicit that credential replacement/removal preserves saved intent and that lack of a credential delays reconciliation rather than deleting or invalidating entries? [Consistency, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK013 Is the GitLab URL-change rule complete about retaining old-instance entries, excluding them from current-instance coverage, and requiring deliberate removal or new selection? [Completeness, Spec §FR-015]
- [ ] CHK014 Are discovery, reconciliation, and save failures specified with actionable but safe outcomes, including the distinction between connection validation and discovery permission? [Completeness, Spec §FR-018]
- [ ] CHK015 Are missing configuration, retired configuration, malformed provider entities, rate limiting, pagination failure, and partial branch failure covered without ambiguous effects on saved or draft scope? [Edge cases, Spec §Edge Cases, FR-018]

## Interaction and Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] CHK016 Are loading, empty, recoverable error, retry, and unaffected-branch behavior defined at the relevant tree-branch level, rather than only as page-wide states? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005, User Story 3 Scenario 3, SC-005]
- [ ] CHK017 Are keyboard accessibility and deep-hierarchy usability sufficiently specific to review consistently for group expansion, selection, and partial-selection indication? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, Constitution Principle XI]
- [ ] CHK018 Is it clear that search covers only currently available/loaded results and cannot hide, remove, or otherwise mutate selected rules? [Consistency, Spec §FR-016, SC-006]
- [ ] CHK019 Does the save workflow define draft versus persisted state, failed-save retention, navigation-away warning, and successful-save behavior consistently? [Completeness, Spec §FR-011, User Story 1 Scenario 7]
- [ ] CHK020 Is the stale concurrent-edit outcome actionable and bounded, with the user required to reload/review rather than having one draft silently win? [Clarity, Spec §FR-020]
- [ ] CHK021 Are the success criteria measurable enough to determine whether navigation can start before a large hierarchy is fully fetched, while still requiring all pages/entities to remain reachable? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK022 Do the independent user-story tests jointly cover saved intent, unavailable/stale entities, large/deep hierarchies, and search without relying on live GitLab behavior? [Coverage, Spec §User Stories 1–3, FR-021]

## Traceability and Boundaries

- [ ] CHK023 Can every persisted field and reconciliation state be traced to a user-visible need, without making mutable display names/paths authoritative identity? [Traceability, Spec §FR-010, Key Entities]
- [ ] CHK024 Are API-visible hierarchy and scope fields limited to safe normalized navigation/selection metadata, with credentials and raw provider data expressly excluded? [Security, Spec §FR-004, FR-018, FR-019]
- [ ] CHK025 Are Feature 004's excluded execution/mining/authentication capabilities stated clearly enough to prevent scope creep during planning and implementation? [Scope, Spec §FR-017, FR-022]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `$speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `$speckit-specify` and `$speckit-clarify`.
- Add findings inline and link to relevant resources or documentation.
